title: Mastering Retinoschisis: Clinical Pathophysiology & Management
summary: Retinoschisis involves the splitting of the neurosensory retina into two distinct layers, representing a spectrum from benign peripheral senescence to sight-threatening X-linked pathology. This guide navigates the diagnostic nuances and management paradigms for both degenerative and congenital forms.

sections.title: Definition & Epidemiology
sections.content: Retinoschisis is defined as the cleavage of the retina into an inner layer (typically including the ILM, nerve fiber layer, ganglion cell layer, and inner plexiform layer) and an outer layer (outer nuclear layer, PR layer, and RPE). Typical Degenerative Retinoschisis (TDR) occurs in ~5-7% of the population over 40 years of age. X-linked Juvenile Retinoschisis (XLJR) has a prevalence of 1:5,000 to 1:25,000, caused by mutations in the RS1 gene.

sections.title: Clinical Features: TDR vs. XLJR
content: TDR: Asymptomatic, often inferior-temporal, immobile bullous elevation.
XLJR: Macular schisis (spoke-wheel pattern), foveoschisis, vitreous hemorrhage.
XLJR: Peripheral schisis in 50% of cases, typically inferior.

sections.title: Red Flags: When to Worry
content: Outer layer breaks + Inner layer breaks = Rhegmatogenous RD.
Rapid expansion towards the posterior pole.
Symptoms of photopsia or shower of floaters (indicates progressive traction).
Presence of full-thickness retinal detachment.

sections.title: Investigations & Workup
content: Step 1: Dilated Indirect Ophthalmoscopy (Identify boundaries).
Step 2: Scleral Depression (Confirm immobility vs. RD).
Step 3: OCT Macula/Periphery (Visualize split layers and pillars).
Step 4: Goldmann Visual Field (TDR shows absolute scotoma; RD shows relative).
Step 5: ERG (XLJR shows b-wave reduction indicating inner retinal dysfunction).

content.explanation: S: Stationary, C: Concave (Inner), H: Holes (Outer), I: Immobile, S: Splitting, I: Inherited (XLJR), S: Silent (TDR)

sections.title: Management Protocol
content: TDR: Observation is standard. No prophylactic laser unless progression to macula.
XLJR: Carbonic Anhydrase Inhibitors (Dorzolamide) to reduce macular cysts.
Surgical: Pars Plana Vitrectomy (PPV) for vitreous hemorrhage or macula-involving RD.
Surgical: Internal limiting membrane peeling if epiretinal membrane co-exists.

sections.title: Key Clinical Pearls
content: In TDR, the inner layer is thin/transparent; the outer layer is thick/granular.
Unlike RD, retinoschisis does not shift with gravity/head position.
The 'Snowflake' appearance (white dots) on the outer layer is pathognomonic for degenerative schisis.
RS1 gene therapy is currently under investigation for early-onset XLJR.
